description:
Snorri/Cayce needs pqueue to provide an authoritative StateStore boundary before Snorri can replace Cayce's internal workflow runtime in production.

Current evidence from sibling snorri, run against pqueue revision a7401c1:
- `cargo run -p snorri-spike-pqueue -- --source-audit --format markdown` passes its audit harness but reports blocking gaps: no public vectorized claimed-work commit, public upsert/ack/finalize do not accept caller request ids, public ack is item-id shaped instead of lease-token claim-ref shaped, backend data-plane envelopes still build `request_id: None`, `QueueIdempotencyCache` is documented as not wired through push/claim/finalize, RESP is worker/interoperability only, and non-work side records/recovery reads are missing.
- `cargo run -p snorri-spike-pqueue -- --prototype --format markdown` proves the public Rust facade can express Snorri input/state/audit/outbox/await records, but only as multiple public operations: upsert input, claim input, upsert state, push audit, upsert outbox, upsert await, ack input. That is not one recoverable transition boundary.

Required pqueue capability:
Expose a public Rust API for a vectorized claimed-work commit suitable for Snorri transition commits. Each vector entry must atomically validate a lease-token-bearing claim reference, apply bounded opaque non-work side-record writes for workflow state and audit, apply ordinary queue lifecycle writes for dispatchable outbox/await/timer work as needed, advance or validate a caller-supplied instance/state fence, finalize the input claim, and return a per-entry outcome. The API must accept caller-supplied request ids so Snorri can derive stable transition request ids from durable workflow inputs and rely on retained replay/conflict/expired outcomes.

Detailed requirements:
- Public Rust facade exposes a native claimed-work commit operation, not only hidden engine ports.
- Commit request includes caller request id or per-entry transition request id; same body replays, different body conflicts, expired idempotency metadata returns a structural expired outcome.
- Commit entries carry a claim reference with item id, lease token, lease expiry, and item version/fence. Public finalization must not depend only on item id.
- Commit validates claim authority and state/item fence inside the same durable boundary as side-record writes and input finalization.
- Backend command-envelope construction propagates request ids instead of building data-plane envelopes with `request_id: None` for this path.
- QueueIdempotencyCache or equivalent retained request-id machinery is wired into the accepted data-plane commit path.
- Side records intended for authoritative state/audit are not ordinary claimable work. Provide generic non-work opaque records, an equivalent documented non-work convention with conformance tests, or a capability-declared adapter-owned table boundary. Outbox effects, due timers, and awaits may remain ordinary queue lifecycle records when claim/finalize semantics are intended.
- Capability descriptors must let Snorri reject unsupported backends before activation: atomic transition commit, vectorized commit, lease validation, retained commit idempotency, non-work side records, authoritative recovery reads, delayed awaits/timers where advertised, and clear durability/consistency boundary.
- Recovery/explain reads expose enough committed records to decide retry/replay and explain instance state: transition request id, workflow instance key/fence, consumed input event id, side-record writes, outbox/await/timer records, and per-entry commit status.
- RESP is explicitly out of scope for authoritative Snorri StateStore MVP unless it grows an equivalent Rust-finalizable claim/ref and request-id commit boundary. RESP can remain worker/interoperability surface.

In-scope areas:
- crates/pqueue/src/lib.rs public facade and public types
- crates/pqueue-engine command envelopes, idempotency, finalize validation, backend write/command composition, and capability descriptors
- memory/sqlite/postgres/objectlog backend data-plane plumbing needed by the new boundary
- projection/recovery reads needed to prove the committed records are visible and replay-safe
- tests/contract fixtures proving the boundary across at least memory and one durable backend

Out of scope for this bead:
- Making pqueue understand Snorri workflow categories such as workflow state, audit, effect, or await. Payloads should stay opaque to pqueue.
- Choosing tenant/job semantics for Snorri or Cayce. Cayce/Snorri create unique queues per workflow/run; pqueue should not need Cayce tenant id or job id beyond opaque queue identity and caller metadata.
- RESP parity for authoritative state commits.
- Cayce-side migration code.
title: Expose Snorri authoritative vectorized claimed-work commit

description: Under CPU starvation / high host load, multi-node object_log_sqlite_projection collapses ~36x (8-owner worst per-queue 3300/s -> 87/s) instead of degrading gracefully. ROOT CAUSE (code-traced): each node runs its own InMemoryControlPlane (sole owner of its disjoint queues). When the background renew_sessions task runs late under load, the lease TTL (15s) lapses; cp_resolve reports Unassigned; the node re-acquires via lease_decide_acquire (control_plane.rs:126) which UNCONDITIONALLY does assignment_epoch+1. That epoch bump fences the node's OWN in-flight pushes/claims (EpochFenced / -ERR pqueue epoch_stale) -> client retry storm -> under continued starvation repeats -> collapse. A slow-but-alive owner fences itself. FIX: re-affirming ownership of one's OWN uncontested lease (current.active_owner == acquiring owner) must PRESERVE assignment_epoch (refresh lease_expires_at only); epoch advances ONLY on takeover by a DIFFERENT owner. Safe: if the authority record still names us active_owner, no other owner acquired in the gap. Result: graceful degradation. Exposed by pqueue-36d405a9's live cargo test failing its 8-owner sweep under host load ~13 on a 12-core box.
title: Ownership self-fencing under load: re-acquiring own lease bumps the fence epoch (no graceful degradation)
